pattern.crimePattern: grandmother kills a water-gang collector who threatened her grandson; the grandson confesses falsely
pattern.notes: Water-vending cartels taxing community water points are a documented pattern in Nairobi settlements; no real gang, committee or incident is depicted. Tone: quiet and sad. The victim is the aggressor; the reconstruction neither glamorises the killing nor mocks him.

ob.reportedBy: Zipporah Mutheu, resident, Mathare North; confession at the front desk by Baraka Kazungu (19)
ob.text: Zipporah Mutheu reports a man, Stanley Mulwa (36), found dead beside community water kiosk MK-7, Mathare North, at 21:50. At 22:00 a young man, Baraka Kazungu (19), walked into the station and confessed to the killing.

people.name: Stanley Mulwa
people.occupation: Collects "fees" from water points for a water-vending gang
people.bio: Walks the river kiosks every week collecting a cut of the takings for the gang he works for. People pay, or things happen.

image.brief: Kenyan man, mid 30s, heavy build, a leather jacket over a vest, a thick gold-coloured chain, a hard smile that is meant to frighten, ID-photo framing

people.name: Kadzo Kahindi
people.bio: Has run kiosk MK-7 for fourteen years for the residents' water committee. Refuses to pay the gang.

image.brief: Kenyan grandmother, late 60s, small and wiry, a faded kanga over her head and shoulders, a bunch of keys on a string, deep lines around a closed mouth, ID-photo framing

people.name: Baraka Kazungu
people.bio: Helps his grandmother at the kiosk. On Monday a man broke his right arm. Tonight he walked into the station and confessed.

image.brief: Kenyan young man, 19, thin, a football jersey with no badge, right forearm in a white plaster cast and a sling, eyes fixed on the floor, ID-photo framing

people.name: Nicholas Ruto
people.bio: Wanted Mulwa's stretch of the river. The two crews have fought before.

image.brief: Kenyan man, early 40s, lean, a black funeral armband on a sports jacket, a hoarse voice from singing, calm and watchful, ID-photo framing

people.name: Zipporah Mutheu
people.bio: Lives in the iron-sheet house next to the kiosk. Her window looks straight onto the tap stand.

people.name: Rhoda Jebet
people.bio: Night-shift nurse at a fictional community clinic. Set Baraka's arm on Monday.

people.name: Rosebella Akinyi
people.occupation: Host of a funeral vigil in Huruma
people.bio: Her brother died on Saturday. The matanga has run every night since.

places.name: Zipporah's house, next to the kiosk

locations.name: Maji Safi Kiosk No. 7 (MK-7), Mathare North
locations.description: A blue water tank on a concrete stand, a tap with a padlocked cage, a painted price board: KSh 5 per 20-litre jerrican. The main valve is opened with a long iron key. Mud everywhere. One bulb.

hotspots.label: By the tap stand
hotspots.text: Stanley Mulwa lies in the mud beside the tap stand. A long iron T-bar lies next to him.

hotspots.label: The iron T-bar
hotspots.text: The valve key: an iron T-bar taller than a child. Pick it up and turn it over.

hotspots.label: Notice on the tank
hotspots.text: A committee notice painted on the side of the tank.

hotspots.label: Counter
hotspots.text: The attendant's sales book on the counter, a pencil tied to it with string.

hotspots.label: House next door
hotspots.text: Zipporah Mutheu stands in her doorway with a jerrican she never filled.

hotspots.label: Price board
hotspots.text: "MAJI SAFI — KSh 5 per 20 L — Mathare North Water Committee." Someone has scratched a different number underneath: 10.

image.brief: a community water kiosk in a Nairobi informal settlement at night, a blue plastic water tank on a concrete stand, a caged tap, a painted price board, yellow jerricans lined up in the mud, a single bulb on a wire, iron-sheet houses close around it, no people in focus

evidence.title: The body by the tap stand

body.note: Report language only. Struck with the kiosk's iron valve key, found in the mud beside him.

image.brief: the muddy ground beside a community water tap stand at night, a long iron T-shaped valve key lying in the mud, spilled yellow jerricans, torchlight, no body visible

body.label: Iron T-bar, about 1.2 m. Painted MK-7. Two worn grip patches on the crossbar: it takes both hands to swing.

image.brief: a long iron T-bar valve key about 1.2 metres long lying on a concrete slab, the letters MK-7 painted on the shaft, two shiny worn grip patches on the crossbar

body.text: VALVE KEY HELD BY KIOSK ATTENDANT ONLY. — Mathare North Water Committee

body.diagnosis: Fracture, RIGHT forearm. POP cast applied.

facts.text: Zipporah Mutheu found Stanley Mulwa dead beside water kiosk MK-7 at 21:50.
At 22:00 Baraka Kazungu, 19, walked into the station and confessed.
Mulwa was struck with the kiosk's iron valve key, which lies in the mud beside him.
The valve key is an iron T-bar about 1.2 m long, painted MK-7. Swinging it takes both hands.
Committee notice: 'Valve key held by kiosk attendant only.' The attendant is Kadzo Kahindi.
Kadzo's sales book: the last sale is at 21:05. Nothing after that, though the kiosk normally sells until 22:00.
Zipporah: from her window she could see Kadzo at the counter from 21:00. Nobody else came to the kiosk until Mulwa at 21:10 and Baraka at about 21:18.
Zipporah: at 21:10 she heard Mulwa at the kiosk shouting, "Next time it's the boy's head."
Zipporah: at about 21:15 she heard a heavy clang, then nothing.
Zipporah: at 21:20 she saw Kadzo walk Baraka away from the kiosk, holding him by the elbow.
Zipporah: Baraka came running from the football pitch at about 21:18, still in his jersey. Her son had sat beside him on the touchline since eight.
Zipporah stayed in her house from 20:30 until she went out for water at 21:50.
Zipporah: Mulwa's crew and Nicholas Ruto's crew have been fighting over this stretch of river all year.
Baraka's clinic card, Monday: 'Fracture, RIGHT forearm. POP cast applied. Review in 6 weeks.' His right arm is in a cast and sling.
Rhoda: on Monday Baraka said "a man" broke his arm over water money. He was too frightened to say who.
Rhoda has been on the clinic's night shift since 19:00.
Baraka: "I did it. I hit him with the valve key. Leave my grandmother out of this."
Baraka admits he was not at the kiosk when it happened. His grandmother called him there after, and told him to go home and say nothing.
Kadzo: "That man broke my grandson's arm on Monday. Because the boy would not give him our takings."
Kadzo: "I sell water. That is all I do."
Nicholas: "I was at a matanga in Huruma all night."
Rosebella: Nicholas Ruto came to her brother's matanga at 20:00 and led the singing until after one in the morning.

interrogations.intro: Baraka sits at the front desk with his cast on the counter. "I already told them. Write it down."

topics.reply: Leave her. She is old. She didn't do anything.

interrogations.intro: Kadzo sits on an upturned jerrican with her hands folded. She does not look at the mud.

topics.reply: Nobody else touches it. The committee says so. Fourteen years, it hangs on my wall.
She goes quiet for a long time. "He is a good boy. He brings me tea."
Monday. Because he would not give that man our takings. Two thousand shillings. For water.

interrogations.intro: Nicholas answers his phone over the sound of singing. "Mulwa? Huh. Everyone on that river had a reason."

topics.reply: Everyone on this river had a reason. Not everyone had the stomach.
Call Mama Akinyi. It is her brother's matanga. I have been leading the songs all night.

interrogations.intro: Zipporah puts down her empty jerrican. "I heard it. I hear everything at that kiosk. These walls are tin."

topics.reply: The nurse at the clinic set the boy's arm on Monday. Ask her what he said.

contradictions.reaction: ...I wasn't there when it happened. Bibi called me after. She told me to go home and say nothing. I couldn't let them take her. She is all I have.

prosecutor.pass: The court will hear what he did to that boy. It still has to hear what she did.
fail: A confession is where you start, not where you stop. Look at his arm.
No. Who holds that key, and who was at that counter when the clang came?

proof.concludes: Baraka could not swing a two-handed iron bar with his right arm in a cast, and he was on the touchline until he came running at 21:18, after the clang. His confession is false, and protects someone who called him to the kiosk afterwards.

The weapon is the valve key only the attendant holds. Kadzo's sales stop at 21:05. Mulwa threatened the boy at 21:10 and was struck at 21:15, and the only other person at the kiosk was Kadzo. Kadzo Kahindi killed Stanley Mulwa.

eliminations.why: Baraka's right arm is in a cast, the key needs two hands, and he was on the touchline at the pitch until he came running at 21:18.
Nicholas was leading the singing at a matanga in Huruma from 20:00 until after one.
Zipporah was in her house next door; she heard, and only came out at 21:50.
Rhoda was on the clinic's night shift from 19:00.

reconstruction.text: Monday. Baraka will not hand over the kiosk's takings. Mulwa breaks his arm. At the clinic Baraka says only, "a man".
Tuesday, 21:05. Kadzo sells her last jerrican of the night.
21:10. Mulwa comes back. He tells her that next time it will be the boy's head.
21:15. She takes the valve key off its hook in both hands and swings it once. He does not get up.
She calls Baraka from the pitch, walks him away by the elbow and tells him to go home and say nothing. At 22:00 he walks into the station instead and says he did it.

tier1.line: Pick the key up. Turn it over. Then look at the boy who says he swung it.

tier2.line: Read the notice on the tank. Then ask the neighbour who was at the counter between ten past and quarter past nine.

glossary.def: Funeral vigil: mourners gather and sing for several nights.
Printed cotton cloth, often with a proverb along the edge.
Mother; also a respectful way to address or name a woman.

ui.beatNotes: Handling objects in 3D: the valve key can be lifted and turned; its two worn grip patches show without any text. First case where a physical property of an object (it needs two hands) is the deduction.
